title: OKR Initiative Compression — prioritizing a minimal cross-functional delivery set
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
Problem: As company-level OKRs consolidate for Q2, teams are proposing a large set of initiatives that collectively exceed available delivery capacity. This ticket creates a playbook and decision flow (the 'compression' process) to surface the minimal set of cross-functional initiatives that still deliver OKR coverage with acceptable risk.

Goals:
1) Define a lightweight, repeatable assessment rubric for initiative inclusion (impact, dependencies, effort, risk).
2) Produce a prioritized, time-boxed minimal delivery set that maps 80%+ of target OKR signal to <= 60% of initiatives.
3) Create a communication & escalation protocol for deprioritized initiatives and resource reallocation.

Scope: Company-level OKRs and initiatives that span >2 teams (Engineering, Product, Design, GTM). This excludes purely team-internal roadmap items.

Out of scope: Detailed sprint plans for individual teams (those will be handled downstream after compression).
acceptance_criteria: Compression rubric documented and reviewed by Exec PM and two cross-functional leads
A candidate minimal initiative set (<= 60% of proposed initiatives) mapped to each company OKR with traceability
Stakeholder signoff from Engineering, Design, Sales, and Customer Success on the compressed plan or documented exceptions
Communication artifacts (email + deck) and escalation path published to Confluence and shared with leadership
A small simulation showing projected capacity utilization and risk delta between full and compressed sets
